items.title: The derived limit of an inverse system of complexes fits into the canonical product distinguished triangle
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an object K = (K_n^bullet) of the derived category of the inverse systems of abelian groups and asserts the existence of a canonical distinguished triangle R lim K -> prod_n K_n^bullet -> prod_n K_n^bullet -> R lim K[1] in D(Ab), which says precisely that R lim K is a derived limit of the inverse system in the sense of the derived-category definition (source lines 23269-23280). The proof splits into a special case and a reduction. In the special case where each inverse system (K_n^p) is right acyclic for lim, the computation lemma gives a short exact sequence 0 -> lim_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> 0 for every p, and since the complex with terms lim_n K^p_n computes R lim K, the lemma holds in that case (proof lines 23283-23291). The substantive step is the reduction: for general K, the computation lemma provides a quasi-isomorphism K -> L in D(Ab(N)) such that each (L_n^p) is acyclic, and because products are exact in the category of abelian groups the product prod K_n^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to prod L_n^bullet; hence the result for L, already proved, implies the result for K (proof lines 23294-23299). The non-routine content is the passage from the acyclic case to the general one using the existence of a suitable replacement and the exactness of products.
